title: Python: K1, *args is a tuple, **kwargs a dict, and an unshadowed builtin class receiver is the builtin (resolved-external; DEC-303 (a22) item 3)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3, group K1, verbatim: 'K1: *args is a tuple and **kwargs a dict, and an unshadowed builtin class used as a receiver is the builtin; all are resolved-external. This refines (a12)(a): a splat first parameter still yields no instance receiver.' Governing line (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope; nonlocal writes in nested scopes count for a local, global writes in the same module for a module-level name. Refined by (a29) item 2 and (a30) item 2: type, and any class with type in its MRO, is outside the exemption (constructing it does not return an instance), and the exemption covers builtin CLASSES only, not every builtins name; an unshadowed builtin class is not opaque for the __new__ rule. Probed on dev 4dd0b473: today def f(*args): args.index(1), def f(**kwargs): kwargs.get(1), int.from_bytes(...), dict.fromkeys(...) and str.join(...) are all receiver-needs-inference (none resolved-external), so K1 is unbuilt. Part of the DEC-303 (a23) build order; releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a call on a *args parameter resolves to resolved-external as a tuple method, and on a **kwargs parameter as a dict method, when every binding of the name is enumerable from the text of its scope (a rebind, or a nonlocal write in a nested scope, leaves it unresolved), with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins

a call through an unshadowed builtin class used as a receiver (int.from_bytes, dict.fromkeys, str.join) resolves to resolved-external, and a shadowed name, type, or a class with type in its MRO stays unresolved
a splat first parameter still yields no instance receiver for self, as (a12)(a) says
each rule has a mutation check that goes red, and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with any in-repo edge it creates or removes named

implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a22) item 3 K1, refined by (a29) item 2 and (a30) item 2). PROBE on dev bd0a977: K1 was unbuilt (every case receiver-needs-inference). Also found: a typed splat parameter (*args: int, **kw: str) parses as typed_parameter > list_splat_pattern|dictionary_splat_pattern > identifier, which parameterName missed, so the name bound NOTHING (a binding-enumeration hole of the D1/D2 kind, and the reason the rule-41d fixture passed by accident). BUILT in src/python/calls.ts: (1) RawBinding.splat records tuple or dict for a *args or **kwargs parameter (def and lambda); parameterName and a new splatKind look through a typed_parameter, and isPlainParameter no longer lets a typed splat be a receiver ((a12)(a) preserved). (2) resolveAttributeCall: one segment on a name whose scope-chain lookup has exactly ONE binding, a splat parameter, is external/external (a rebind, for, with-as, annotated assignment or a nonlocal write from a nested scope is a second binding and leaves it receiver-needs-inference); read from a nested function works. (3) resolveBareName external outcome with one segment and a name in isBuiltinClassName (BUILTIN_INSTANCE_CLASSES, builtin exception classes, plus the receiver-only bool, range, slice, memoryview, reversed) is external/external; type and non-class builtins (len) stay unresolved; shadowing, a partial star import and a longer chain stay unresolved. The tuple-versus-dict distinction is recorded but not observable in a bin (both are external), so it is informational. The four existing tests that pinned a splat first parameter call as receiver-needs-inference (rule 32 x3, rule 41d) now pin resolved-external with the same no-instance-receiver and no-in-repo-edge assertions. FIXTURES: describe K1 in test/python-calls.test.ts, 7 tests (splat resolves incl. typed, lambda and nested read; no in-repo edge and no instance receiver with a positive twin; second-binding refusals with a twin; plain parameter, two segments and keyword-only refused; builtin class receivers; shadowed, type, len, chain, star import, class-body shadow refused; a class with type in its MRO refused with a dict-base twin). RED BEFORE: 4 of 7 fail on the dev source. MUTATION CHECKS, 11 mutants each red: splat resolution off, any binding count, any param kind, multi segments (splat), builtin class receiver off, multi segments (builtin class), every builtins name, receiver-only classes off, typed splat as receiver, typed splat name off, typed splat kind off. PER-SITE MEASURE, instrumented origin/dev bd0a977 vs the branch, five pins, multiset diff: 78 sites move receiver-needs-inference to external, 0 in-repo edges created or removed, 0 other changes (flask 23, jinja 23, httpx 18, rich 3, tqdm 11; by a coarse source-text split about 18 builtin-class receivers (object.__new__, int.__new__ and similar) and the rest *args/**kwargs receivers). NOT MEASURED: precision on labelled sites, the sites of the tuple/dict distinction. Gates: typecheck, lint, format:check, bun test 835 pass.

REVIEW ROUND 1 (Opus, #165 at af73bbc0), amends the build note: (1) a typed splat annotated with an in-repo class was a wrong in-repo edge: knownClassOf read the annotation of *args: C as the class of args, so args.index(1) got an edge to C.index; fixed by ignoring the annotation of a splat binding in knownClassOf (it types the elements, not the tuple or dict); twins for *args: C, **kw: C and a typed splat first parameter in a method, with a plain annotated parameter still resolving. (2) a shadowed builtin class name passed the K1 branch through an alias: int = type; int.mro(C) went resolved-external; fixed by gating on isUnshadowedBuiltin(base.name); twins int = type, int = len, a local dict = len. (3) a name bound anywhere in the starting class body is read from the class or the globals, never an enclosing function, so a later import in the class body no longer lets a splat parameter qualify (the underlying rule 38 fall-through is unchanged and predates this PR). The 'type in its MRO' fixture is carried by E1's instanceClassOf, not by a K1 branch. MUTANTS now 14, each red (the build note said 11; added: knownClassOf splat guard off, builtin receiver unshadowed gate off, class body binding guard off). Per-site measure re-run: still 78 sites receiver-needs-inference to external, 0 in-repo edges created or removed, none from defect 1. bun test 837 pass.

REVIEW ROUND 2 (Opus, #165 at 185a6ebf): a splat parameter read through a scope that declares global for the same name read the module, not the function, and lookupBindings never consults globalNames (a global with no write in the reading scope moves nothing). Fixed in isSplatParameter only: refuse when any scope from the starting scope up to but not including the scope holding the parameter has the name in globalNames. Refused fixtures: a global in a nested function with a module-level args, and a global in a class body with none; twins: a read-only nonlocal (really reads the parameter) and no global at all, both still external. object.__new__(C) added to the builtin-class receiver fixtures. 15 mutants, each red (added: global between use and parameter off). Per-site re-measure unchanged: 78 sites receiver-needs-inference to external, 0 in-repo edges created or removed. FOLLOW-UPS, named and not fixed here (both predate this PR and the root cause is outside K1): (a) lookupBindings never consults globalNames, so rule 6d knownClassOf has the same shape for x: C when a nested scope declares global x with no write; (b) rule 38 ignores loops, so in a class body a use before a later import inside a for loop is read as the enclosing binding on the first iteration but as the import on the second.
